newsitem.title: INDIA: Higher tariffs hit India Tata Electric Cos.
newsitem.headline: Higher tariffs hit India Tata Electric Cos.

text.p: Higher tariffs imposed by a state-run electricity board squeezed the profits of Tata Electric Companies (TEC) in the year ended March 31, 1997, the firm said in a statement on Thursday.

"The companies have taken the interests of the consumers into account and absorbed a large part of this increase while continuing to maintain operating efficiency under difficult conditions," the statement said.
The Maharashtra State Electricity Board raised tariffs to TEC effective October 1, 1996 which increased its costs by 990 million rupees in 1996/97 (April-March), it said.
TEC's net profit fell to 2.3 billion rupees in 1996/97 from 4.4 billion a year ago, but distributable profit were higher at 2.2 billion against 1.7 billion.
"The increased distributable profits were mainly due to the companies making lower statutory and special appropriations," the TEC statement said.
Statutory and special appropriations were lower at 136.7 million rupees against 2.76 billion in 1995/96.
TEC comprises three firms: The Tata Hydro-Electric Power Supply Co Ltd, The Andhra Valley Power Supply Co Ltd and Tata Power Company Ltd.
TEC took over a thermal power station from Tata Iron and Steel Company Ltd in January 1997 when the first unit of 67.5 megawatts was tested and commercial operations began shortly after, it said.
The plant will have a total capacity of produce 307.5 megawatts, it added.
